p1: In 1919, a serial killer wrote to a newspaper... and promised to spare every home playing jazz.
New Orleans, 1918. Someone was breaking into homes at night.
He chiselled through the door... and let himself in.
Then he used the family's own axe.
At least six people were killed.
Then, in March 1919, the Times-Picayune printed a letter.
The writer called himself a demon from the hottest hell.
He named the night: Tuesday, at 12:15.
And one promise: any home with a jazz band playing would be spared.
That night, the whole city played jazz. Bars and cafes were packed.
And that night... nobody was killed.
But it didn't stop him. He struck again that same year.
To this day, nobody knows if that letter was really his... or who he was.
He was never caught. Just like the letter said.
